newsitem.title: ALBANIA: IMF, WBank urge quick Albania action on investment.
newsitem.headline: IMF, WBank urge quick Albania action on investment.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund and World Bank have urged Albanian authorities, with a week to go in an election campaign, to take quick action to regulate investment schemes after collapses triggered mass unrest.
A letter sent by the heads of the IMF and World Bank at the weekend asked President Sali Berisha to sign into law as quickly as possible a decree on controlling the operations of such schemes.

Five "pyramid" investment schemes collapsed earlier this year, swallowing up the life savings of hundreds of thousands of investors with little awareness of financial markets after 45 years of eastern Europe's harshest Communist regime.
At least 1,500 people have died in violence which engulfed the country in March and prompted the dispatch of a 7,000-strong "Multinational Protection Force".
Four other schemes remain in operation but have ceased paying the high interest rates initially promised.
The proposed legislation was initially approved by parliament but later amended after the IMF and World Bank expressed reservations about its provisions.
It must now be passed by presidential decree as parliament is in recess ahead of next Sunday's legislative elections.
The process has been slowed by a row pitting Berisha against Prime Minister Bashkim Fino -- a member of the Socialist Party challenging the president's Democratic Party in next Sunday's election.
Berisha wants monitoring procedures to extend to the four failed schemes. The Socialists say those schemes must be dealt with by the courts.
The IMF has disbursed about $60 million in credits to Albania since 1992, but loans were suspended in 1995. The World Bank has provided nearly $300 million in credits.
Berisha's Democrats won a huge majority in last year's general election criticised in Albania and abroad as unfair. This time they face a stiff challenge from the Socialists.
